Issued at 124 AM EDT Fri Oct 16 2026

Current Weather through Friday:

The Ohio Valley will be going through a significant pattern change 
over the next 24 hours as a mature low pressure system continues to 
push eastward within an amplified positively tilted upper level 
trough. The orientation of this trough created a less aligned 
phasing of the mid to lower level low of which has created a 
multitude of weaker boundaries out ahead of the primary cold front 
and a slower arrival of polar air. One of these confluence 
boundaries was the initiation point for a broken line of strong to 
severe thunderstorms this afternoon and evening. As of 04Z, this 
line has weekend significantly with only scattered showers remaining 
over far E/SE Indiana. 

Another area of low level confluence can be observed over NW Indiana 
and E Illinois, of which will be the source for additional showers 
and isolated weak thunderstorms tonight into tomorrow morning. 
Lapse rates within this sector of the low are weak in the mid levels 
of which should keep convective tops capped below 15kft and the 
thunder threat very isolated. 

The surface low will continue to mature overnight within strong 
upper level jet dynamics. In return, CAA will continue to increase 
pushing the cold front quickly E/SE passing through central Indiana 
between 09-13Z. A few showers will be possible along the frontal 
passage, but any additional QPF should be less than 0.1". 

For the remainder of the day, central Indiana will be within a much 
cooler airmass with dew points in the 40s and high temperatures in 
the mid to upper 50s. Modest lapse rates up to 850mb will likely 
lead to efficient PBL mixing in the afternoon with gusts upwards of 
40 MPH. A few isolated showers cannot be ruled out as saturation at 
the top of the PBL remains coincided with the previously 
mentioned steep low level lapse rates; that said, any QPF will be 
minimal. As the late afternoon and evening approaches, mean low 
level winds back towards 330-360 degrees, of which provides an 
efficient fetch across Lake Michigan. While a majority of any lake
effect rain showers will likely remain north of central Indiana, 
isolated to scattered showers over NW portions of the area will 
remain possible from 21- 01Z. 


Friday Night through Sunday Morning: 

The remainder of the forecast period will become rather stagnant as 
the upper low associated with today's trough passage will detach 
from the flow and become cutoff over the Eastern Coast. This in 
combination with a weak split flow upper jet will keep low level 
conditions fairly similar through the weekend and into next week. 
While the bulk of the forecast will remain similar, slight 
fluctuations in surface pressure over the next 5-7 days will still 
lead to slightly different temperatures and wind speed/direction 
over the forecast period. 

Continued CAA Friday night will lead to cold morning lows Saturday 
morning, but there is some uncertainty on the extent of any frost 
given consistent 6+ MPH surface winds and marginal temperatures 
around 36-38 degrees. Greatest chances will be within sheltered 
areas in NE portions of central Indiana, but likelihood of occurrence 
is currently below 50%. The aforementioned strong CAA will lead to 
height rises beneath 850mb and therefor building high pressure 
Friday night through most of Saturday. The centroid of this surface 
high is expected to overlap with the core of the mid level polar 
airmass late Saturday though Saturday night leading to our coldest 
temperatures of the season. Frost looks definite for most of central 
Indiana on Sunday morning, but there is still some significant 
uncertainty in below freezing temperatures. Much of this will depend 
on the timing of the surface high passage along with how it faces 
with the 850mb temperatures. Ensemble probabilities indicate greater 
around a 50% chance for NE/E portions of the area, which will be the 
focus for any freeze headlines in later updates. 

Remainder of Sunday through Wednesday: 

The anticyclone will drift eastward toward the Mid-Atlantic on 
Sunday, allowing insolation to rebound highs into the upper 50s and 
lower 60s. Lows Sunday night will remain cool, in the upper 30s to 
lower 40s, with patchy frost confined to far eastern rural valleys 
before low-level winds back to the south.

For Monday through Wednesday, the synoptic pattern transitions as 
upper-level ridging builds over the eastern states and a deep trough 
carves out over the western CONUS. Steady south-southwesterly return 
flow will drive a significant warm air advection regime across the 
Ohio Valley. 850 mb temperatures will moderate to +10C to +13C, 
pushing daytime highs into the upper 60s and lower 70s by early next 
week. Overnight lows will moderate into the upper 40s to mid-50s.
